original_sources_are_aggregator_autogene.detail: All search results for 'carrier onboarding and compliance platform market size' return only Growth Market Reports, MarketIntelo, and Dataintelo — the same cluster of auto-generated aggregator reports. These three domains appear to re-package the same underlying model estimates with minor variation ($1.30B, $1.42B, $1.54B, $1.62B in 2024 across their multiple product variants) with no disclosed methodology. They do not constitute independent cross-validation. Bloomberg NEF, Gartner, McKinsey, BCG, Roland Berger, and multilateral bodies do not publish a 'carrier onboarding and compliance platform' sub-market figure.

descartes_corporate_filings.conclusion: Descartes Systems (DSGX) is the dominant listed company in the carrier onboarding/compliance niche. FY2025 total revenue was $651M ($572.9M in FY2024), reported as a single segment with no sub-breakdown for carrier onboarding specifically. Descartes acquired MyCarrierPortal in September 2024 for ~$24M (+ up to $6M earn-out) — implying MCP's trailing revenue was in the low-to-mid single-digit millions, far below what would anchor a $1.54B+ global market for this specific niche.

gartner_scm_market_total.conclusion: Gartner's SCM software market (broader: all supply chain management software) was ~$33.4B in 2024 (+12.4% YoY). This is the total market for SCM software globally and is not broken out by 'carrier onboarding and compliance.' Carrier onboarding/compliance is a narrow sub-niche of TMS/freight compliance within SCM; a plausible sub-segment share would be in the 3–7% range of TMS revenue, which is itself a sub-segment of SCM. No Gartner document provides a carrier-onboarding specific sub-market size.

mckinsey_roland_berger_bcg.conclusion: No authored report found from McKinsey, BCG, Bain, or Roland Berger specifically sizing a 'carrier onboarding and compliance platform' market. Roland Berger's FreightTech White Paper (2020) is qualitative, covers freight technology broadly, and does not estimate this sub-segment. McKinsey's digital logistics report discusses technology investment trends but provides no market-size figure for carrier compliance specifically.

apac_submarket_340m.conclusion: The APAC $340M figure originates solely from Growth Market Reports. No independent source found. The only corroborating signals are: (a) Gartner's Descartes APAC geographic revenue of $18.2M in FY2024 — a fraction consistent with APAC being an early/small market, but Descartes is just one vendor; (b) general Asia-Pacific digital freight adoption trends from ADB and World Bank publications which do not quantify this sub-segment.

descartes_segment_data_as_anchor.note: The MCP acquisition price (~$24M) and Descartes' single-segment reporting are the best available primary-data anchors for this niche. Standard M&A SaaS multiples of 3–6x ARR would imply MCP had $4M–$8M in annual recurring revenue. If Descartes (via Highway, Carrier411, MCP, MacroPoint FraudGuard) controls ~10–20% of a market estimated at $1.54B–$1.62B, Descartes' carrier compliance-attributable revenue would need to be $154M–$324M. No filing confirms a segment at this scale — the entire company is $651M across all logistics services globally, with carrier compliance being one small part.
descartes_segment_data_as_anchor.internal_consistency_assessment: The $1.54B–$1.62B figure appears significantly overstated for 'carrier onboarding and compliance platforms' as a distinct sub-market. The $20B 'broader freight broker software' figure (vc-6) is arguably more consistent with the Gartner SCM total; the carrier compliance sub-niche is likely a fraction of that.
